stem: Add \(5.55 \times 10^4\) and \(6.95 \times 10^3\), expressing the result in scientific notation.
solution:
For adding \(5.55 \times 10^4\) and \(6.95 \times 10^3\), first the exponent is made equal. Thus

\(5.55 \times 10^4 + 0.695 \times 10^4\). Then these numbers can be added as follows :

\((5.55 + 0.695) \times 10^4 = 6.245 \times 10^4\)
_note: p-01 right column, first pink box. The book prints NO `Solution :` label for Problems 2.1-2.4: the box is one continuous run of text that both poses and works the item. Split here at the natural seam — the imperative is the stem, the printed run is the solution verbatim. Nothing is dropped.

stem: Perform the subtraction \(3.5 \times 10^{-2} - 5.8 \times 10^{-3}\), expressing the result in scientific notation.
solution:
The subtraction of two numbers can be done as shown below:

\(3.5 \times 10^{-2} - 5.8 \times 10^{-3}\)

\(= (3.5 \times 10^{-2}) - (0.58 \times 10^{-2})\)

\(= (3.5 - 0.58) \times 10^{-2}\)

\(= 2.92 \times 10^{-2}\)
_note: p-01 right column, second pink box. No printed `Solution :` label — see the note on Solved Ex.2.1.

stem: In laboratory experiment, 10 g potassium chlorate sample on decomposition gives following data ; The sample contains 3.8 g of oxygen and the actual mass of oxygen in the quantity of potassium chlorate is 3.92 g. Calculate absolute error and relative error.
solution:
The observed is 3.8 g and accepted value is 3.92 g

Absolute error \(=\) Observed value \(-\) True value

\(= 3.8 - 3.92 = -0.12\ \mathrm{g}\)

The negative sign indicates that your experimental result is lower than the true value.

The relative error \(= \dfrac{\text{Absolute error}}{\text{True value}} \times 100\%\)

\(= \dfrac{-0.12}{3.92} \times 100\% = -3.06\%\)
_note: p-02 right column. The `10 g potassium chlorate` in the stem is not used anywhere in the printed working; transcribed as printed.

stem: The three identical samples of potassium chlorate are decomposed. The mass of oxygen is determined to be 3.87 g, 3.95 g and 3.89 g for the set. Calculate absolute deviation and relative deviation.
solution:
mean \(= \dfrac{3.87 + 3.95 + 3.89}{3} = 3.90\)

**Average deviation of a set of measurements**

| Sample | Mass of oxygen | Deviation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.87 g | 0.03 g |
| 2 | 3.95 g | 0.05 g |
| 3 | 3.89 g | 0.01 g |
| Mean absolute deviation | | 0.03 |

Absolute deviation \(= |\,\text{Observed value} - \text{Mean}\,|\)

\(\therefore\) Mean absolute deviation \(= \pm 0.03\ \mathrm{g}\).

The relative deviation,

\(= \dfrac{\text{Mean absolute deviation}}{\text{Mean}} \times 100\%\)

\(= \dfrac{0.03}{3.9} \times 100\% = 0.8\%\)
_note: p-03 left column. The book's table is reproduced as a GFM pipe table; its `Mean absolute deviation` row leaves the middle cell empty, as printed.

stem:
Round off each of the following to the number of significant digits indicated :

a. 1.223 to two digits

b. 12.56 to three digits

c. 122.17 to four digits

d. 231.5 to three digits.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: two defects in the book's printed answer to this worked example. (i) The question labels its four items a, b, c, d while the answer list labels them i, ii, iii, iv — the two are in the same order, so i corresponds to a and so on. (ii) The reasoning for item iii reads "the fifth digit is greater than 5, so we **do** it and add 1 to the fourth digit"; the intended word is **drop**, as it is in items i, ii and iv. All four rounded values — 1.2, 12.6, 122.2 and 232 — are correct.]

i. 1.2; the third digit is less than 5, so we drop it all the others to its right.

ii. 12.6 ; the fourth digit is greater than 5, so we drop it and add 1 to the third digit.

iii. 122.2 ; the fifth digit is greater than 5, so we do it and add 1 to the fourth digit.

iv. 232; the fourth digit is 5, so we drop it and add 1 to the third digit.
_note: p-04 left column. Transcribed verbatim, INCLUDING two printed defects: the stem labels its items a-d while the answer list labels them i-iv, and item iii reads 'we do it' where 'we drop it' is meant. Both carried to errata.

stem: A compound contains 4.07 % hydrogen, 24.27% carbon and 71.65 % chlorine by mass. Its molar mass is 98.96 g. What is its empirical formula ? Atomic masses of hydrogen, carbon and chlorine are 1.008, 12.000 and 35.453 u, respectively
solution:
[Textbook misprint: in Step III the book prints the divisor for carbon as 12.01 g, contradicting the atomic mass of 12.000 u its own stem supplies. The printed value 2.0225 is what 12.000 gives (24.27/12.000 = 2.0225); 12.01 would give 2.0208. So the divisor is the misprint and the value is right. The answer is unaffected either way — the H : C : Cl ratio is 2 : 1 : 1 and the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4Cl_2}\) on both readings. The same 12.01 recurs in the empirical formula mass 49.48; with 12.000 it is 49.47, and the ratio 98.96/49.47 is still 2.]

**Step I :** Check whether the sum of all the percentages is 100.

\(4.07 + 24.27 + 71.65 = 99.99 \approx 100\)

Therefore no need to consider presence of oxygen atom in the molecule.

**Step II :** Conversion of mass percent to grams. Since we are having mass percent, it is convenient to use 100 g of the compound as the starting material. Thus in the 100 g sample of the above compound, 4.07 g hydrogen 24.27 g carbon and 71.65 g chlorine is present.

**Step III :** Convert into number/of moles of each element. Divide the masses obtained above by respective atomic masses of various elements.

Moles of hydrogen \(= \dfrac{4.07\ \mathrm{g}}{1.008\ \mathrm{g}} = 4.04\)

Moles of carbons \(= \dfrac{24.27\ \mathrm{g}}{12.01\ \mathrm{g}} = 2.0225\)

Moles of chlorine \(= \dfrac{71.65\ \mathrm{g}}{35.453\ \mathrm{g}} = 2.021\)

**Steps IV :** Divide the mole values obtained above by the smallest value among them. Since 2.021 is smallest value, division by it gives a ratio of 2:1:1 for H:C:Cl.

In case the ratio are not whole numbers, then they may be converted into whole number by multiplying by the suitable coefficient.

**Step V :** Write empirical formula by mentioning the numbers after writing the symbols of respective elements. \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl}\) is thus, the empirical formula of the above compound.

**Step VI :** Writing molecular formula

**a. Determine empirical formula mass :** Add the atomic masses of various atoms present in the empirical formula.

For \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl}\), empirical formula mass is

\(12.01 + 2 \times 1.008 + 35.453 = 49.48\ \mathrm{g}\)

**b. Divide molar mass by empirical formula mass**

\(\therefore\ \dfrac{\text{Molar mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}} = \dfrac{98.96\ \mathrm{g}}{49.48\ \mathrm{g}}\)

\(\therefore r = 2\)

**c. multiply empirical formula by r obtained above to get the molecular formula.**

Molecular formula \(= r \times\) empirical formula

molecular formula is \(2 \times \mathrm{CH_2Cl}\) i.e. \(\mathrm{C_2H_4Cl_2}\).
_note: Spans p-04 right column ('Contd on next page') into p-05 left column. Transcribed verbatim, INCLUDING the printed divisor 12.01 g in Step III, which contradicts the stem's stated atomic mass 12.000 u; the printed VALUE 2.0225 is what 12.000 gives (24.27/12.000 = 2.0225), while 12.01 gives 2.0208 — so the divisor is the misprint, not the value. Carried to errata; the answer is unaffected.

stem: A compound with molar mass 159 was found to contain 39.62 % copper and 20.13 % sulfur. Suggest molecular formula for the compound (Atomic masses: Cu = 63, S = 32 and O = 16).
solution:
% copper + % sulfur \(= 39.62 + 20.13 = 59.75\)

This is less than 100 % Hence compound contains adequate oxygen so that the total percentage of elements is 100%.

Hence % of oxygen \(= 100 - 59.75 = 40.25\%\)

Moles of Cu \(= \dfrac{\%\ \text{of Cu}}{\text{Atomic mass of Cu}} = \dfrac{39.62}{63} = 0.629\)

Moles of S \(= \dfrac{\%\ \text{of S}}{\text{Atomic mass of S}} = \dfrac{20.13}{32} = 0.629\)

Moles of O \(= \dfrac{\%\ \text{of O}}{\text{Atomic mass of O}} = \dfrac{40.25}{16} = 2.516\)

Hence the ratio of number of moles of Cu:S:O is

\(\dfrac{0.629}{0.629} = 1\), \(\dfrac{0.629}{0.629} = 1\) and \(\dfrac{2.516}{0.629} = 4\)

Hence empirical formula is \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\)

Empirical formula mass \(= 63 + 32 + 16 \times 4 = 159\)

Molar mass = Empirical mass (Since Molar mass = Molecular mass)

\(\therefore\) Molecular formula = Empirical formula \(= \mathrm{CuSO_4}\)
